title: The First Benefit Period an Allowance Is Owed For
content:
The first benefit period for which a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card is owed an allowance is taken from the medical plan that carries the card where that plan's cover began within the benefit year, and from the programme's own opening otherwise.

**The rule.** The first benefit period the allowance is owed for is the benefit period the medical plan carrying the card began cover in, where that plan's cover began after the first day of the benefit year; it is the first benefit period of the benefit year, where that plan's cover began on the first day of the benefit year; and it is the benefit period the programme opened in in every other case.

**Which records decide it.** The medical plan carrying the card is the member's enrollment in the Medicare Advantage Health Plans, and the day its cover began is the coverage effective day carried on that enrollment. The benefit period a day falls in is found by counting the whole months from the first day of the benefit year to that day and dividing by the months in a benefit period.

| The medical plan's cover | The first benefit period the allowance is owed for |
|---|---|
| began after the first day of the benefit year, at least 1 whole month into it | the benefit period that cover began in |
| began on the first day of the benefit year | the first benefit period of the benefit year |
| no such enrollment stands | the benefit period the programme opened in |

**Worked through on hypothetical dates.** On a card whose benefit period runs 3 months, a medical plan whose cover began 4 whole months into the benefit year: the first period the allowance is owed for is the second quarter of the year. A plan whose cover began on the first day of the benefit year: the first period of the year. A card with no medical plan enrollment standing, whose programme opened 7 whole months into the year: the third quarter of the year.
